answer: Two ravens carrying the same seal down the river belong to one operator, and the atlas registry voids both at settlement. Each identity registers one seal at the river's source, backed by an 850,000 POA stake, and a raven carries it to the atlas at payout. The atlas checks every seal: a duplicate burns both rewards, both stakes pass to honest peers, and the operator pays a 400,000 POA fine per fake. One fake costs 1,250,000 POA, and five fakes cost 6,250,000 POA before any payout clears.
